description: It has no face, only appetite. The ringed mouth opens wider than reason, and the light goes in first.
lore: Look at the body before you look at the mouth. Four legs, a working shoulder, a tail with a switch in it — the whole frame of something that once grazed and was nervous of dogs. Then the neck ends in rings of teeth around a hole, and there is no face on it anywhere, no part of the head a name could ever have gone into. It keeps to bare grey rock, the high stone where nothing comes up at all. Violet marks crawl over the hide and give off their own light, the one colour on a hillside that has none, and ordinary light goes the other way: hold a torch out toward one and it lights your hand and nothing past it. In every account of one there is not a single line of it putting its head down. A grazer's body that has never grazed.

There are three words for what a creature is here and not one of them will sit on this. It did not come — nothing that grazed anywhere arrives shaped like that. It was not made; the made are pooled out of what crowds of the dead agree on, and there is no crowd anywhere that agrees on this. And Hollowed means a thing emptied out and left with its outside, the outside being the whole of what the Hollowed keep. This one did not keep a face. The guides file it under Hollowed because a guide has to put a thing somewhere, and the crackers who work that stone will tell you plainly that the guides are guessing.

[[characters/8c41be1e|Hearn]] does not discuss [[lore/the_hole_under_the_mountain|the mountain]]. Everyone knows why and everyone asks anyway. Shown an account of one of these, he broke his own rule for it: not the mountain's work, he said, and then a second sentence nobody had asked for — that the thing under the mountain wants something, and this wants nothing at all, it only opens. He would not go further. His reason was never the Chronicle. People who believe a thing came out of the mountain go east after it, and Hearn has been east once, with company, and does not mean to be why anyone goes again.
gm_notes: The taxonomy genuinely does not cover this one and the record says so out loud rather than inventing a fourth kind; the kind field reads hollowed because the schema has three slots and a guide has to file it somewhere, exactly as the text admits. Leave it unresolved — an open question of this shape is worth more than an answer. It takes LIGHT, never memory: B16 (something other than the hole also takes memory) belongs to Nightmare alone and must not be doubled up here. Hearn's second sentence is the hinted B7 material only (it wants something, it is not hateful) and goes no further. Ground is data-driven: maps2 placed it on stone in MONSTER_HABITAT and the text followed, which sharpened rather than cost it — a grazer's frame standing where nothing grazes is the taxonomy problem made visible, and the violet is the only colour on grey rock.
